title: Lamb chops with new potatoes, spinach and Bramley

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food: potatoes, onions, spinach, garlic, lamb chops, apples, oil, rosemary and wholegrain mustard.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a standard Tesco line, and lamb chops, though not the cheapest meat, are an ordinary weeknight buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large roasting tray, a knife and a board, and uses simple roasting.

works.reason: Setting the chops on 400g of raw spinach in a tray already full of potatoes means the spinach floods the tray as it wilts, so in 10 to 12 minutes the chops steam grey rather than brown, and the last step's mixing of apple, juices and spinach under the chops is muddled.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for halving the potatoes, cutting onion wedges, slicing garlic and coring the apples, and 25 + 12 + 5 matches the 42 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Each name matches its id, every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: April spinach with new potatoes and lamb suits mid-spring, and 400g of spinach is a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British English with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a balanced family dinner of lamb, potatoes, greens and fruit.
